summary.prose: This Story adds the read-only models.definitions request: it projects the daemon's model registry into one answer listing every family with its models, aliases, efforts, limits, tier defaults, summariser, tool-loop default, rejected ids and, for Ollama models, whether they are installed. providers.listModels keeps its request and result shape but is computed from that same projection, so the two always agree; for Ollama it lists only listed models that are installed. The temporary getCuratedCatalog accessor s1 kept is removed.

hldContextSlice.frameworkSummary: The curated cloud catalog keeps its file (src/assets/models/cloud-model-catalog.json), its loader (validateModelCatalog, src/daemon/model-catalog.ts:162) and its boot hook (src/daemon/index.ts:381), as the DEF decided, and is extended in place; the boot hook moves ahead of the settings reconcile and the worker threads, because the settings defaults now come from the file. The file is extended into the model definitions: exactly one entry for each built-in family, each with its CLI kind (CLI families), its selectable models with aliases, accepted efforts and input limit, its tier defaults and summariser model (CLI families), the Ollama tool-loop default, and the default family. Each Ollama model's input limit is its context window and replaces the global models.shaper.ollamaNumCtx; the output cap ollamaNumPredict stays global. A ModelRegistry built from the file and the per-user approved-model store answers every model question in the daemon; each thread builds it on first use and caches it, the way it loads and caches settings today (src/config/analyze.ts:234). A daemon restart guarantees that every thread uses a changed file, approval or saved tier; until then, a thread that starts or first reads them after the change, such as a worker the supervisor replaces after a crash (src/daemon/threads/supervisor.ts:136-148), may already use it, as with settings today. That is harmless: every saved tier has passed config.write's checks and every approval a check in which the model ran. The settings catalog takes the defaults of its tier runner, tier model and local coreModel rows, and the allowed effort values, from the same file, so reconcile, the updater, the settings catalog loader and older plugins keep working unchanged and no model name stays in code. One read-only request, models.definitions, serves the definitions to clients and is the source of providers.listModels; models.resolveRole lets the TUI's review command run the model the daemon would. Unknown Claude and Codex models are checked through their CLI one call at a time and recorded only on the user's approval, and only for a check in which the model ran. A tier set to a model that is neither listed nor approved runs a tier default with a warning (decision A). Tiers become global-only; a repo keeps `tasks` and coreFloor. Every Story leaves the build and tests passing, keeping a named stopgap for anything a later Story migrates. Settings-write safety is out of scope (ISSUE-8dc75bc5).

ownedContracts.name: models.definitions IPC request
ownedContracts.purpose: The one read-only request clients use to learn the definitions (k2): families with CLI kind and rejected ids, models with aliases, efforts and limits and whether they are shipped or user-approved, tier defaults, summariser model, tool-loop default, default family, and each listed Ollama model's installed state. providers.listModels is drawn from the same registry (s2/ac2).

consumedContracts.name: ModelDefinitionsFile (the curated catalog file, extended)
consumedContracts.purpose: The shipped, versioned data format of src/assets/models/cloud-model-catalog.json: the only place model facts and default model choices are stated (k4). Validated at daemon start (k7); a change applies at the next restart (s1/ac2). Ollama models must be listed to be selectable.

consumedContracts.name: ModelRegistry and the approved-model store
consumedContracts.purpose: The in-process view every daemon consumer asks, built from the sc1 file plus the per-user approved-model store and cached per thread like settings. Defines the store's entry shape (written by s4). Resolves aliases, accepted efforts, input limits and defaults, and applies decision A.

boundary.internal: The models.definitions handler and its method-class entry, the projection of the registry, each listed Ollama model's installed state from the existing bounded listing, and re-sourcing providers.listModels from the registry (for Ollama, listed models only), then removing the curated catalog accessor s1 kept. Tests: models.definitions returns every field of a fixture file (ac1); providers.listModels and models.definitions agree for every family, and an installed but unlisted Ollama model appears in neither (ac2); with Ollama not answering, installed is absent and the request still succeeds.

adjacentBoundaries.internal: Extending the catalog file, its types (CloudModelCatalogFile, src/daemon/model-catalog.ts:48) and its validator in place; refreshing its contents with today's models, the aliases today's tier defaults use (opus, sonnet, haiku), the Ollama models insrc ships with and their context windows, and today's coreModel as the tool-loop default; the registry and its per-thread cache; moving the boot validation ahead of the settings reconcile and the worker threads; reading the approved-model store (a malformed store is logged and treated as empty); keeping the curated catalog's existing accessor answering providers.listModels from the new file shape until s2 replaces it. The validator refuses a missing or malformed file, an unknown, missing or repeated family, a CLI family without its CLI kind, tier defaults or summariser model, a model without an efforts list, a duplicate id or alias, a default that is not a model of its family, an Ollama model without a token input limit, and a tool-loop default that is not listed, naming the entry (ac3). Tests: one fixture per refusal reason (ac3); a model and alias added to a fixture are served after a restart with no code change (ac2); the file is validated before the settings reconcile, before any worker starts and before listen (ac1, k7); repeated requests in one thread return the same definitions even after the file changes on disk (ac1); a replacement worker started after the file, the store or config.json changed on disk uses the new values while a surviving thread keeps its own until the restart, and a thread whose first read comes after such a change likewise uses the new values; after a daemon restart every thread resolves the same definitions, approvals and tiers; providers.listModels still returns today's Claude and Codex models through the kept accessor; alias, effort and limit lookups; resolveTier distinguishes rejected-model from unlisted-model and falls back to the tier's family default, or the default family's for an Ollama tier.

Moving every daemon consumer onto the registry: tier resolution, summariser selection, effort forwarding, CliProvider's input budget and CLI kind, OllamaProvider's num_ctx, the tool-loop model (an unlisted coreModel runs the tool-loop default with a warning) and the runner and model literals in routing, provider construction, attribution and workflow code; SUMMARISER_CLI_FALLBACK, CODEX_INPUT_BUDGET_CHARS and ollamaNumCtx go; DEFAULT_TIERS and TIER_EFFORTS stop being written in code and remain only as temporary exports drawn from the definitions for the TUI's model-tiers pane, which s5 migrates; no daemon code uses them. The settings catalog's tier and coreModel defaults and effort values are taken from the definitions; how the settings catalog reaches the file is decided in this Story's LLD and must work in every process that loads the settings catalog today (the daemon, the TUI, the updater, and the VS Code bundle until s6 drops its use). Reconcile removes per-repo tier overrides with a warning and prunes ollamaNumCtx; readRepoOverride and its callers go. config.write refuses a tier set to a rejected model and reports restartRequired. models.resolveRole and its method-class entry. Both installer copies take tier defaults and the tool-loop default from the file. Tests: an unset tier resolves to the file's default, and with a fixture whose defaults differ from today's, reconcile fills the fixture's values (ac1); an unsupported effort is dropped with a warning naming model and effort (ac2); a source scan fails on runner or model literals outside the family implementations, on any read of ollamaNumCtx, and on any daemon use of the temporary DEFAULT_TIERS or TIER_EFFORTS exports (ac3); the TUI still builds and its model-tiers pane shows the definitions' defaults; a repo's `tasks` choice applies with the global tier's model (ac4); reconcile removes per-repo tier overrides with a warning naming repo and tier and keeps `tasks` and coreFloor (ac5); an unlisted model falls back with the warning (decision A); a fixture Ollama model's input limit sets num_ctx; config.write refuses a rejected model and reports restartRequired; models.resolveRole matches the daemon's own resolution for a CLI tier and an Ollama tier; the settings catalog loader accepts the catalog and an unset JetBrains tier still shows the default family's values.

The per-family check procedures (Codex: the CLI's model list plus a run; Claude: a run, the input limit from the JSON output, recognised effort names), run one call at a time; telling a reachable CLI that refuses the model apart from an unreachable CLI; refusing approval unless the model ran without error; writing the store atomically and acknowledging a decision only once it is written; the method-class entries. Tests: checks against fake CLIs record each verdict and run one at a time (ac1); results list each claimed level with evidence and nothing is usable before approval (ac2); after approval and a restart only the approved levels are accepted (ac3); a rejected profile or unreachable CLI refuses the model with a reason, and approving a check whose model did not run is refused (ac4); after a restart an approved model appears in models.definitions as user-approved and a rejected one among the rejected ids (ac5); a failed store write returns write-failed and keeps the previous store.

The TUI model-tiers pane and its effort choices from models.definitions, removing the temporary DEFAULT_TIERS and TIER_EFFORTS exports s3 kept; the unknown-model check and approval screen; the repo settings view limited to `tasks` and coreFloor; showing restartRequired and offering maintenance.restart; the review command using models.resolveRole and building its provider from the answer instead of reading config.json; Setup recommending the definitions' tool-loop default instead of DEFAULT_LOCAL_MODEL, and saying it cannot recommend when the daemon is not running. Tests: the pane offers exactly the options of a fake models.definitions answer and no source file still exports or imports DEFAULT_TIERS or TIER_EFFORTS (ac1); saving an unknown model starts the check and shows its results (ac2); the repo view edits only `tasks` and coreFloor (ac3); the review command runs the model a fake models.resolveRole returns for a CLI and an Ollama tier; Setup recommends the fake answer's tool-loop default.

The VS Code model-tier picker driven by models.definitions instead of its runner list and the bundled settings catalog's effort rows, removing the bundle's import of the settings catalog; the unknown-model check and approval prompt; the Repo Configuration panel without per-tier fields; showing restartRequired and offering insrc.daemon.restart. Tests: the picker offers exactly a fake answer's options and the bundle keeps no runner or model list (ac1); an unknown model is saved only after approval (ac2); the repo panel shows only `tasks` and coreFloor (ac3).

The JetBrains model-tiers section driven by models.definitions instead of ModelTiersModel.PROVIDERS; the unknown-model check and approval dialog; the per-repo settings without per-tier fields; showing restartRequired. Tests: the section offers exactly a fake answer's options and the plugin keeps no runner or model list (ac1); an unknown model is saved only after approval (ac2); the per-repo settings show only `tasks` and coreFloor (ac3).

hldContextSlice.rolloutPhase: Phase B — daemon serves and runs by the definitions

nonFunctional.performance: The file is parsed once per thread and every model question is an in-memory lookup; models.definitions touches no CLI and makes one bounded Ollama listing call, the same one providers.listModels makes today.
nonFunctional.security: No cloud REST call is added (k1): checks run only through the installed claude and codex CLIs. The approved-model store is a per-user file under the insrc home written only by the daemon; clients reach it only through models.approve and models.reject (k2).
nonFunctional.observability: A bad file stops the daemon with a log naming the entry (s1/ac3); a dropped effort logs model and effort (s3/ac2); a tier fallback logs tier, requested model, reason and the default used (decision A); a tool-loop substitution logs both models; removing a per-repo tier override logs repo and tier (s3/ac5); each CLI call of a check and its verdict is logged.
nonFunctional.durability: Approved and rejected profiles live outside the shipped file and config.json, so they survive restarts and updates; the store is replaced atomically and a decision is acknowledged only once written; a malformed store is logged and treated as empty. When an update ships a model the user had approved, the shipped definition wins. Existing `tasks`, coreFloor, ollamaNumPredict and every tier value already in config.json are kept. Between a change and the next restart, threads may differ (a replaced worker or a late first read uses the new values); the restart brings them together.

api.name: models.definitions
api.signature: 'models.definitions': (params: unknown) => Promise<ModelDefinitionsResult>  // implemented by modelDefinitions(deps?: ListModelsDeps) in src/daemon/model-definitions.ts

parameters.name: params
parameters.purpose: Ignored; the request takes no parameters (sc3 params: {}).

returns.meaning: The sc3 answer: version and defaultFamily from the validated file; one entry per family in file order with id, cliKind (CLI families), displayName, tierDefaults and summariserModel (CLI families), toolLoopModel (ollama), rejectedModels (CLI families: the registry's effective rejected ids that the family does not serve, possibly empty) and models in registry order, each with id, aliases (always a list, [] when none), displayName when set, efforts, inputLimit when set, source, and installed (ollama models only, and only when the Ollama listing answered).

preconditions: validateModelCatalog has succeeded in this thread (boot validates before listen), so getModelRegistry() returns without throwing.
postconditions: Reads only getModelRegistry() and the validated file's version, and calls the bounded Ollama listing (OllamaProvider.listLocalModels, 4 s) exactly once.

installed is true for an Ollama model whose id equals an installed name exactly and false otherwise; when the listing rejects (unreachable, timeout, malformed) installed is absent on every Ollama model and the request still succeeds.
An installed Ollama model that is not listed does not appear.
Mutates nothing; registered in buildHandlerRuntime's RPC map and as a session method in src/daemon/threads/method-class.ts.

A rejected id that the family also serves (a model the user rejected that a later shipped file lists) is served as shipped and left out of rejectedModels, matching the registry, where find() returns the shipped model and resolveTier uses it; the shipped definition wins (HLD durability).

api.name: listModels
api.signature: listModels(params: unknown, deps?: ListModelsDeps): Promise<ModelListResult | ListModelsError>

parameters.name: deps
parameters.purpose: Injected seams: ollamaList() (the bounded listing) and registry() (getModelRegistry) plus catalogVersion() (the validated file's version); default to the real ones.

returns.meaning: Unchanged shape. For a CLI family: available:true and every model the definitions answer lists for that family (shipped then user-approved) as { id, displayName? }. For ollama: when the listing answers, available:true and the listed models whose installed is true; when it does not, available:false and [].

errors.condition: provider missing or not one of the three families: { error: 'invalid-params: ...', recoverable: false }, as today.

preconditions: validateModelCatalog has succeeded in this thread.
postconditions: Builds its answer from the same projection models.definitions uses, so for every family its models equal the definitions answer's models for that family (ollama: those with installed === true) mapped to { id, displayName? }.
A CLI-family request does not call the Ollama listing.
No longer reads getCuratedCatalog, which is removed.

dataModelChanges.details: The IPC answer type exactly as the HLD sc3 sketch, exported for the handler and tests. Projection rules: families and models keep registry order; aliases is always a list; optional fields are omitted rather than set to undefined (exactOptionalPropertyTypes); rejectedModels = the ids in registry.rejected(family) that registry.find(family, id) does not resolve, on CLI families only (a shipped model wins over a rejected profile; the registry contract is unchanged).
dataModelChanges.schemaDiff: + interface ModelDefinitionsResult { version; defaultFamily; families: { id; cliKind?; displayName; tierDefaults?; summariserModel?; toolLoopModel?; rejectedModels?; models: { id; aliases; displayName?; efforts; inputLimit?; source; installed? }[] }[] }

+ registry(): ModelRegistry

dataModelChanges.details: Adds ['models.definitions', 'session', false]; the admin and indexing counts the coverage test pins are unchanged. The handler-map test's sorted RECORDED_RPC list gains 'models.definitions' in the same change.

interactionWithShared.howDetails: Owns the models.definitions request and its ModelDefinitionsResult, and derives providers.listModels from the same projection (s2/ac2).
Reads families(), defaultFamily(), models(), rejected() from getModelRegistry(); no registry change.
Reads only the version from validateModelCatalog()'s cached file (the registry has no version accessor).

errorCases.scenario: Ollama does not answer the listing during models.definitions (unreachable, the 4 s timeout, or a malformed reply).
errorCases.detection: The injected ollamaList() promise rejects; the projection catches the rejection.
errorCases.response: Builds the answer without installed on any Ollama model and returns it as a success; nothing is logged at warn level beyond what the listing already logs.
errorCases.userImpact: Clients still see every family and model; they cannot tell which Ollama models are installed until Ollama answers.

errorCases.scenario: Ollama does not answer during providers.listModels for 'ollama'.
errorCases.response: Returns { provider: 'ollama', available: false, models: [] }, exactly as today.
errorCases.userImpact: Pickers show Ollama as unavailable, as they do today.

errorCases.scenario: providers.listModels is called with a missing or unknown provider.
errorCases.detection: extractProvider finds no valid provider in params.
errorCases.response: Returns the existing invalid-params ListModelsError without touching the registry or Ollama.
errorCases.userImpact: The client gets the same error it gets today.

errorCases.scenario: The registry cannot be built in the serving thread (definitions file bad).
errorCases.response: Not reachable in a running daemon: boot validates the file before listen (s1). If it ever happened, the error propagates to the RPC dispatcher's existing error reply; neither handler catches it.
errorCases.userImpact: None in practice; the daemon would not have started with a bad file.

edgeCases.input: An installed Ollama model that is not listed in the definitions (for example llama3:8b).
edgeCases.expected: Appears in neither models.definitions nor providers.listModels('ollama').

edgeCases.input: A listed Ollama model installed under a different tag (listed qwen3.6:27b, installed qwen3.6:latest).
edgeCases.expected: installed is false for qwen3.6:27b; matching is exact string equality, no tag normalisation.

edgeCases.input: Ollama answers with zero installed models.
edgeCases.expected: models.definitions marks every Ollama model installed: false; providers.listModels('ollama') returns available: true and [].

edgeCases.input: A model with no aliases in the file.
edgeCases.expected: aliases is [] in the answer, never absent.

edgeCases.input: A user-approved Codex model in the store (after s4).
edgeCases.expected: Listed after the shipped Codex models with source 'user-approved' in models.definitions, and included in providers.listModels('cli-codex').

edgeCases.input: A rejected Codex model that the file does not list.
edgeCases.expected: Appears only in the cli-codex family's rejectedModels; absent from models and from providers.listModels.

edgeCases.input: A model the user rejected that a later shipped file lists under the same id (catalog-update collision).
edgeCases.expected: Served as shipped: it appears in models with source 'shipped' and in providers.listModels, and is left out of rejectedModels, as the registry already resolves it.

edgeCases.input: models.definitions called with params null, {} or extra keys.
edgeCases.expected: Params are ignored; the same answer is returned.

edgeCases.input: providers.listModels for a CLI family while Ollama is down.
edgeCases.expected: Unaffected: available: true with the family's models; the Ollama listing is not called.

invariantsToPreserve.text: providers.listModels keeps its request ({ provider }) and result ({ provider, available, models: [{ id, displayName? }] }) shapes, with available:false + [] for an unreachable Ollama, because the VS Code picker and the JetBrains gateway parse it until s6/s7 move them to models.definitions.
providers.listModels is a read-only session method dispatched through buildHandlerRuntime; it makes no cloud REST call and mutates nothing.
The method-class table lists exactly the methods buildHandlerRuntime serves; a new handler gets its entry in the same change, and the admin/indexing counts stay as pinned.

migration.stateBefore: providers.listModels (src/daemon/handler-runtime.ts:1430 -> listModels, src/daemon/list-models.ts:100) answers CLI families from the s1 stopgap getCuratedCatalog().modelsFor (src/daemon/list-models.ts:83-86), which lists only shipped models, and answers Ollama with every installed model from the bounded listing (src/daemon/list-models.ts:74-78, src/agent/providers/ollama.ts:265), listed or not. There is no models.definitions request; the method-class table has no entry for it (src/daemon/threads/method-class.ts:150 holds providers.listModels as session).
migration.stateAfter: models.definitions returns the sc3 projection of getModelRegistry() with each listed Ollama model's installed state, registered as a session method. providers.listModels keeps its request and result shape and is computed from the same projection: CLI families list shipped then user-approved models; Ollama lists only listed models that are installed, and available:false + [] when Ollama does not answer. getCuratedCatalog, CuratedCatalog and CatalogModel no longer exist.

migrationSteps.action: Add src/daemon/model-definitions.ts with the ModelDefinitionsResult type and the projection over the registry, the file version and an optional installed list.

Register 'models.definitions' in buildHandlerRuntime's RPC map, add ['models.definitions', 'session', false] to the method-class table, and add it to RECORDED_RPC in src/daemon/__tests__/handler-runtime.test.ts, in the same change.
Switch listModels' deps from catalog() to registry() and catalogVersion() and compute its answer from the projection (CLI families without calling the Ollama listing).
Remove getCuratedCatalog, CuratedCatalog and CatalogModel (and CloudProvider if unused) from src/daemon/model-catalog.ts, and update the model-catalog and model-registry tests that used them.
Rewrite list-models.test.ts for the new deps and add model-definitions tests, the agreement test and the real-daemon integration test.

migration.backwardCompat: providers.listModels keeps its request and result shape, so the VS Code picker and the JetBrains gateway keep working unchanged. Two answers change by design (HLD s2 boundary): providers.listModels('ollama') no longer returns installed models the definitions do not list (an unlisted installed model was never usable as a tier after s3, decision A), and CLI families may include user-approved models once s4 can write approvals (none exist before s4). models.definitions is additive. getCuratedCatalog was internal to the daemon; its only production caller is list-models.ts, changed in the same step.

alternativesConsidered.name: One projection, list derived from it
alternativesConsidered.oneLineSummary: A new model-definitions module projects the registry into the sc3 answer; providers.listModels is computed from that same answer.
alternativesConsidered.approach: Add src/daemon/model-definitions.ts with modelDefinitions(deps): it reads getModelRegistry() and the validated file's version, calls the existing bounded Ollama listing once, and projects every family into the sc3 ModelDefinitionsResult (Ollama models carry installed only when the listing answered). listModels(params, deps) in src/daemon/list-models.ts keeps its request and result shape but takes its models from modelDefinitions' answer for the requested family: CLI families map every served model (shipped and user-approved) to {id, displayName?} with available:true; Ollama maps the listed models whose installed is true, and returns available:false with [] when the listing did not answer, as today. Register 'models.definitions' in buildHandlerRuntime and the method-class table as a session method. Remove getCuratedCatalog, CuratedCatalog and CatalogModel from model-catalog.ts and the catalog dependency from list-models.ts.
pros: One projection serves both requests, so they agree by construction (ac2), not only by test.
Reuses the registry, the bounded Ollama listing and the existing handler/method-class pattern; adds one module.
Keeps providers.listModels' request and result shape unchanged for the VS Code and JetBrains clients until s6/s7.
cons: providers.listModels for a CLI family now builds the whole answer, including the Ollama listing call it does not need (a 4 s bound at worst) unless the deps let it skip the listing for CLI families.

alternativesConsidered.name: Two projections over the registry
alternativesConsidered.oneLineSummary: models.definitions and providers.listModels each read the registry directly with their own mapping.
alternativesConsidered.approach: Add a models.definitions handler that projects the registry into the sc3 answer. Change listModels to read getModelRegistry().models(family) for CLI families and to filter the Ollama listing by registry.find('ollama', id) for Ollama, without going through the definitions answer. Remove getCuratedCatalog. Register the new method in the handler map and the method-class table.
pros: providers.listModels for a CLI family makes no Ollama call.
Each handler stays small and independent.
cons: Two mappings of the same registry can drift (for example over user-approved models or installed state); ac2 agreement holds only as long as a test keeps them aligned.
Duplicates the Ollama installed-state logic in two places.
alternativesConsidered.reasonRejected: Equal on ac1 and sc3 but only partial on ac2: the installed-state and model mapping are written twice and can drift.
